reply_text:
*I’d hold the merge.* Reviewed `slug-validation` at `e8612a7` against `main` at `9ba0eca`. Two issues:

1. *[P1] Validation accepts a valid substring, not the whole slug* — `src/validate.js:1–4`
   `/[a-z0-9-]+/` accepts anything containing at least one allowed character. Confirmed that `Hello`, `hello world`, `a/b`, `../admin`, and `"hello\n"` all pass and produce page paths. Encoding afterward doesn’t enforce the documented slug rules.
   *Recommendation:* enforce a full-string match, including rejection of trailing line terminators. Add negative tests for uppercase, whitespace, slashes, dots, punctuation, and newlines.

2. *[P1] Reserved slugs are never rejected by the page route* — `src/route.js:1–5`
   `isReserved` is implemented but never called by either the validator or `pagePath`. All four reserved names still produce paths: `/p/new`, `/p/edit`, `/p/admin`, and `/p/api`, contrary to the README’s route-reservation guarantee.
   *Recommendation:* enforce reserved-name rejection in the page-path validation flow and test all four through `pagePath`, not just the helper.

*Verification:* All 4 existing tests pass, but they miss both issues. I reproduced both with direct calls. No code changed.
